formulas.title: The five answers
formulas.prompt: What are the five standard answers in a bank-paper "compare x and y" question?
formulas.formula:
x > y   x < y   x ≥ y   x ≤ y
x = y or the relationship cannot be established
formulas.explanation: Pick the one that holds for every pair of an x value and a y value.
formulas.example: x = 3 or 4 and y = −4 or −5: every x beats every y, so x > y.
formulas.commonMistake: Choosing x > y when only the larger roots are compared.
formulas.applicationPrompt: x = 2 or 5, y = 3 or 4. Which answer?

formulas.title: Split the middle term
formulas.prompt: How do you factorise a·v² + b·v + c quickly?
formulas.formula:
Find p and q with p × q = a × c and p + q = b,
then v = −p/a and v = −q/a
formulas.explanation: Writing b·v as p·v + q·v lets the expression factor in pairs.
formulas.example: 2x² − 7x + 6: product 12, sum −7 → −3 and −4, so x = 3/2 and 2.
formulas.commonMistake: Forgetting to divide by a, so 3/2 becomes 3.

formulas.title: Compare every pair
formulas.prompt: With two x values and two y values, how do you decide the answer?
formulas.formula:
Put all the roots on a number line:
all x right of all y → x > y; all x left of all y → x < y
touching at one point → ≥ or ≤; overlapping → cannot be established
formulas.explanation: The relation must hold whichever root x and y actually take.
formulas.example: x = 3 or 5, y = 3 or 4: x = 5 > 4 but x = 3 < 4, so the relationship cannot be established.

formulas.title: v² = k and v = √k
formulas.prompt: How many values does x² = 81 give, and how many does y = √81 give?
formulas.formula:
v² = k → v = +√k or −√k (two values)
v = √k → v = +√k only (one value)
formulas.explanation: The square-root sign always means the positive root.
formulas.example: x² = 64 gives ±8; y = √64 gives 8. So x ≤ y.

formulas.title: Root signs from the coefficients
formulas.prompt: In x² + bx + c = 0, how can you tell the signs of the roots without solving?
formulas.formula:
c positive, b positive → both roots negative
c positive, b negative → both roots positive
c negative → one positive, one negative
formulas.explanation: The roots multiply to c and add to −b.
formulas.example: x² − 7x + 12: both positive. y² + 9y + 20: both negative. So x > y without solving fully.
formulas.commonMistake: Reading the root signs as the same as the signs in the equation.

formulas.title: Roots are the bracket numbers, sign flipped
formulas.prompt: Once x² − 7x + 12 is written as (x − 3)(x − 4), what are the roots?
formulas.formula: Roots = the numbers in the brackets with their signs changed

levels.title: Comparing x and y
levels.description: The bank-paper question type: solve two equations and choose from five fixed answers.

blocks.title: The question type
blocks.body: Bank prelims (IBPS, SBI) set about five of these in every paper. Statement I gives values of x, statement II gives values of y, and you choose one of five fixed answers. Most take under a minute once you know the routine.

blocks.title: The five answers
blocks.body:
x > y   x < y   x ≥ y   x ≤ y
x = y or the relationship cannot be established
blocks.caption: Choose the one that is true for every pair of an x value and a y value.

blocks.title: The routine
blocks.body: x² − 7x + 12 = 0 gives x = 3 or 4. y² + 9y + 20 = 0 gives y = −4 or −5. Every x is above every y, so x > y.
Signs first: a positive constant with a negative x term means both roots are positive; with a positive x term, both negative. Often that settles the answer before you finish factorising.

questions.question: Which relation between x and y is true?

table.caption: Solve both equations, then compare x and y

options.text: x = y or the relationship cannot be established

questions.explanation: I: (x − 3)(x − 4) = 0, so x = 3 or 4. II: (y + 4)(y + 5) = 0, so y = −4 or −5. Every x is greater than every y: x > y. The signs alone tell you: both x roots positive, both y roots negative.
questions.method: Find every value of x and of y, then compare each pair.

hints.text: Look at the signs: what do they say about each pair of roots?

commonMistakes: Taking the roots of II as +4 and +5.

questions.question: Which relation between x and y is true?

table.caption: Solve both equations, then compare x and y

options.text: x = y or the relationship cannot be established

questions.explanation: I: x = −2 or −3. II: y = 1 or 2. Every x is less than every y: x < y.
questions.method: Find every value of x and of y, then compare each pair.

hints.text: Both x roots are negative; both y roots are positive.

commonMistakes: Reading the x roots as +2 and +3.

questions.question: Which relation between x and y is true?

table.caption: Solve both equations, then compare x and y

options.text: x = y or the relationship cannot be established

questions.explanation: x² = 64 gives x = 8 or −8. y = √64 means only the positive root, 8. x is either equal to y or below it: x ≤ y.
solutionSteps: x = 8 = y or x = −8 < y, so x ≤ y.
questions.method: Find every value of x and of y, then compare each pair.

hints.text: How many values does each statement give?

commonMistakes: Giving y the value −8 too, which would make the answer "cannot be established".

questions.question: In a "compare x and y" question, when is the answer "x = y or the relationship cannot be established"?

options.text: When some x value is above some y value and another is below, or when x and y are equal
Whenever one of the equations has two roots
When every x is greater than every y

questions.explanation: The answer must hold for every pair of an x and a y. If the pairs disagree, no single relation holds; if x and y are simply equal, this choice also covers it.
solutionSteps: Compare each x with each y.
Mixed results, or exact equality, → this choice.
questions.method: The chosen relation must be true for every pair.

hints.text: Think about x = 3 or 5 against y = 4.

commonMistakes: Choosing it whenever the question looks hard.

questions.question: Which relation between x and y is true?

table.caption: Solve both equations, then compare x and y

options.text: x = y or the relationship cannot be established

questions.explanation: I: 2x² − 7x + 6 = (2x − 3)(x − 2), so x = 3/2 or 2. II: (y − 2)² = 0, so y = 2. x is 2 (equal) or 1.5 (smaller): x ≤ y.
questions.method: Find every value of x and of y, then compare each pair.
commonMistakes: Answering x < y and missing that x can equal 2.

questions.question: Which relation between x and y is true?

table.caption: Solve both equations, then compare x and y

options.text: x = y or the relationship cannot be established

questions.explanation: I: x = 3 or 5. II: y = 3 or 4. x = 5 is above both y values, but x = 3 equals one and is below the other. The pairs disagree, so the relationship cannot be established.
questions.method: Find every value of x and of y, then compare each pair.

hints.text: Put all four roots on a number line.

commonMistakes: Comparing only the larger roots (5 > 4) and answering x > y.

questions.question: Which relation between x and y is true?

table.caption: Solve both equations, then compare x and y

options.text: x = y or the relationship cannot be established

questions.explanation: I: x = −5 or −6. II: y = −3 or −4. All four are negative, so the signs alone do not decide it; but every x is below every y: x < y.
questions.method: Find every value of x and of y, then compare each pair.

hints.text: Both sets are negative: compare the actual values.

questions.question: Which relation between x and y is true?

table.caption: Solve both equations, then compare x and y

options.text: x = y or the relationship cannot be established

questions.explanation: I: 3x² − 10x + 8 = (3x − 4)(x − 2), so x = 4/3 or 2. II: y = 1 or 3. x = 2 is above y = 1 but below y = 3: cannot be established.
questions.method: Find every value of x and of y, then compare each pair.

questions.question: Which relation between x and y is true?

table.caption: Solve both equations, then compare x and y

options.text: x = y or the relationship cannot be established

questions.explanation: I: (x − 4)(x + 3) = 0, so x = 4 or −3. II: (y + 3)² = 0, so y = −3. x is either above y (4) or equal to it (−3): x ≥ y.
questions.method: Find every value of x and of y, then compare each pair.

hints.text: II is a perfect square, so y has one value.

commonMistakes: Answering x > y and missing the equal pair.

questions.question: Which relation between x and y is true?

table.caption: Solve both equations, then compare x and y

options.text: x = y or the relationship cannot be established

questions.explanation: Solve the pair together. Doubling the first gives 4x + 6y = 28; subtracting the second gives 4y = 12, so y = 3 and x = (14 − 9) ÷ 2 = 2.5. So x < y.
questions.method: Find every value of x and of y, then compare each pair.

hints.text: These are two linear equations in the same x and y: solve them together.

commonMistakes: Treating each equation as if it gave x or y alone.

questions.question: Which relation between x and y is true?

table.caption: Solve both equations, then compare x and y

options.text: x = y or the relationship cannot be established

questions.explanation: I: (2x − 1)(3x − 2) = 0, so x = 1/2 or 2/3. II: (3y − 1)(4y − 1) = 0, so y = 1/3 or 1/4. Every x is above every y: x > y.
questions.method: Find every value of x and of y, then compare each pair.
commonMistakes: Inverting the fractions when dividing by the leading coefficient.

questions.question: Which relation between x and y is true?

table.caption: Solve both equations, then compare x and y

options.text: x = y or the relationship cannot be established

questions.explanation: x³ = 729 has one real value, x = 9. y² = 81 gives y = 9 or −9. x equals y or is above it: x ≥ y.
solutionSteps: x = 9 (a cube has one real root).
questions.method: Find every value of x and of y, then compare each pair.

hints.text: A cube root has one real value; a square root has two.

commonMistakes: Giving x two values, ±9, which would make it "cannot be established".

questions.question: Which relation between x and y is true?

table.caption: Solve both equations, then compare x and y

options.text: x = y or the relationship cannot be established

questions.explanation: I: (2x + 7)(x + 2) = 0, so x = −7/2 or −2. II: (2y + 7)(y + 4) = 0, so y = −7/2 or −4. The smallest x (−3.5) equals the largest y, and every other pair has x above: x ≥ y.
solutionSteps: Smallest x = largest y, so x ≥ y.
questions.method: Find every value of x and of y, then compare each pair.
commonMistakes: Missing the shared root and answering x > y.
